recognize_zh: 骨髓切片呈大片壞死，細胞輪廓模糊，其中散布金黃至橘褐色、呈放射狀或菱形團塊的結晶沉積物，即血紅質分解產物 hematoidin，常見於骨髓壞死或舊出血處。
features: Panel A (low power): bone trabecula surrounded by extensive necrotic marrow with loss of cellular detail and scattered golden-brown deposits
Panels B and D: golden-yellow to orange-brown pigment forming radiating, needle-like/spiky crystalline aggregates
Panel C: multiple smaller globular and crystalline golden deposits within amorphous eosinophilic necrotic debris
Background of ghost cells, karyorrhectic nuclear debris and pale eosinophilic granular material
No hemosiderin-laden macrophages or viable tumor cells are clearly identified in these fields
describe_en: Bone marrow trephine biopsy shows extensive marrow necrosis with ghost-cell outlines, karyorrhectic debris and eosinophilic granular material surrounding bone trabeculae. Scattered throughout are extracellular golden-yellow to orange-brown refractile deposits forming radiating needle-like and rhomboid crystalline aggregates, characteristic of hematoidin (bilirubin-derived pigment formed in hypoxic areas of old hemorrhage). Viable tumor is not identified in these fields, and additional sampling or immunostains may be needed to identify an underlying malignancy. Findings are consistent with bone marrow necrosis with hematoidin crystal deposition.

ddx.vs: Hemosiderin is coarse granular golden-brown pigment within macrophages that stains with Prussian blue, whereas hematoidin forms extracellular crystals that are Prussian blue negative.
Formalin pigment is fine, dark brown-black, birefringent and evenly scattered over red cells, not large golden radiating crystals.
Melanin is fine brown-black granular pigment within tumor cells that bleaches and stains with Fontana-Masson, unlike extracellular golden crystals in necrosis.
Charcot-Leyden crystals are bipyramidal eosinophilic (not golden) crystals associated with eosinophils.
